main_text.p: satietatem bibitis, sed non ad ebrietatem: induimini, ita tamen, ut nemo calefiat, & qui se ipsum pro precio elocat, recipit mercedem in saculum pertusum. Et mox. Respicitis ad multum, & ecce parum, quodque in domum infertis, in illud ego infio, ob idscilicet, dicit Dominus exercituū, quod domus mea adhuc deserta est, vos autem curritis, ut quisque domum suam habeat. Idcirco cœli super vos rorem non dant, nec terra prouentum suum. Ego quoque vocaui siccitatem super terram, & super montes, super frumetum & vinum, super oleum, & super vniuersum quod terra profert, super hominem, & super iumentum & super vniuersum laborem manuum.

Periurium & pauperū oppresiio.Quod Deus propter periurium & oppressionem pauperum, cum aliis poenis, tum caritate annonæ homines castiget, ostendit insignis illa historia, quæ 2.Sam.21.cap.extat. Fame dominante tribus annis, consulebat Dauid Dominum quænam tāti mali causa esset, is respondebat famem: eam nāq; gras-sari propter Saulem eiusque domum, quod miseros

page.notes: No page number, catchword or signature is printed. The page is a continuation: the first paragraph begins mid-sentence. The second paragraph breaks off at the foot of the page and goes on to the next. "oppressionem" is written whole because the line break shows no printed hyphen. The marginal note is printed over several lines and is written here as one note. The reading "pauperū" in the note is taken from the scan and may be a worn or doubtful macron.
